newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy tells Turkey of concern on human rights.
newsitem.headline: Italy tells Turkey of concern on human rights.

text.p: Italy told President Suleyman Demirel on Tuesday that it was concerned about Turkey's human rights record and hoped it would improve in view of the country's hopes to join the European Union.
Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni outlined Italy's concern in talks with Demirel, who is on a two-day visit to Italy, a government statement said.
"The Deputy Prime Minister...expressed concern for human rights interventions which have caused worry and emotion in public opinion and in the Italian parliament," it said.
Veltroni told Demirel he hoped the Turkish government would take "specific care" to ensure that human rights abuses were avoided, the statement said.

"He reminded him that Italy and Europe are watching the affirmation of human rights and their adjustment to European standards in view of a gradual move closer by Turkey to the European Union, which Italy looks on with favour," it added.
It said Demirel had explained Turkey's efforts to ensure stability in its region and to deepen its ties with the EU.
The European Parliament, angered by what it sees as Turkey's broken promises to improve human rights, vowed last month to block hundreds of millions of dollars of aid to Ankara.
Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro said on Monday at a state dinner with Demirel that he hoped a peaceful solution could be found to Turkey's conflict with Kurdish separatists.

"Rome is convinced that...the goodwill and far-sightedness of all interested parties make possible the definitions of equitable solutions which respect the rights of all in whatever controversy," Scalfaro said.
"Belonging to the European family means above all else sharing the patrimony of the civil, moral and political values of Europe," he added.

The 15-nation EU, which Turkey hopes to join by the end of the century, appealed to Ankara's Islamist-led government over human rights in July, when 12 people died in a hunger strike over prison conditions.

Turkey entered into a lucrative customs union with the EU last January, but the agreement was held up until Turkey gave explicit guarantees it would take positive action on human rights, democratisation, Cyprus and the plight of the Kurds.
